options: An identifier that already means something in the real world, like a source system's ProductID or an email address
A meaningless, system-generated integer with no business meaning
A key that can never be used in a JOIN
A key that only exists in fact tables, never dimensions
questions.explain: Natural (business) keys carry real-world meaning, unlike surrogate keys.

options: A meaningless, system-generated identifier — almost always a simple incrementing integer — that exists purely to identify a row
Another name for a foreign key
A key that must always be a string, never numeric
The same thing as a natural key, just a different name
questions.explain: Surrogate keys have no business meaning outside the table they identify.

questions.q: In AdventureWorksDW2014's DimProduct, which column is the surrogate key and which is the natural key?
options: ProductKey is the surrogate key; ProductAlternateKey is the natural key carried over from AdventureWorks2012's ProductID
ProductAlternateKey is the surrogate key; ProductKey is the natural key
Both columns are surrogate keys
Neither column is a key of any kind
questions.explain: ProductKey is the warehouse's own auto-generated integer; ProductAlternateKey preserves the original source system identifier.

questions.q: Why does a Type 2 slowly changing dimension require a surrogate key rather than the natural key as the primary key?
options: A primary key can't repeat, so using the natural key would make it impossible to have multiple historical version rows for the same real-world product
Natural keys are always too long to index
Type 2 SCDs technically don't require any kind of key at all
Surrogate keys are required by SQL Server for every table regardless of SCD type
questions.explain: The surrogate key can be unique per version while the natural key repeats across those same versions — exactly what Type 2 history needs.

questions.q: Besides enabling Type 2 history, what is another practical benefit of surrogate keys in a warehouse?
options: They're typically smaller and faster to join on than a natural key, and insulate the warehouse from changes to a source system's own key format
They eliminate the need for any dimension tables
They make CHECK constraints unnecessary
They automatically normalize a table to 3NF
questions.explain: A narrow INT surrogate key is cheaper to join on, and doesn't have to change just because a source system's natural key format changes.
